questions.question: In the following table, fill out if the virus is RNA/DNA, and whether it is enveloped or not. For each virus, name one antiviral that has activity against it, if any (Mumps is given as an example). Table columns: Virus, RNA or DNA, Enveloped (Yes or No), Antiviral. Viruses listed: Mumps, Measles, Hepatitis B, EBV, Influenza, Zika, Ebola.

parts.text: Fill out the table for RNA/DNA, enveloped status, and antiviral for: Mumps, Measles, Hepatitis B, EBV, Influenza, Zika, Ebola

questions.model_answer: Mumps (example): ssRNA (negative-sense), enveloped; no specific antiviral (supportive care). Measles: ssRNA (negative-sense), enveloped; no specific antiviral (supportive care; ribavirin used off-label in severe cases). Hepatitis B: partially double-stranded DNA, enveloped; antivirals - tenofovir or entecavir. EBV: double-stranded DNA, enveloped; no specific approved antiviral (ganciclovir/valganciclovir used off-label for select EBV-driven disease). Influenza: ssRNA (negative-sense, segmented), enveloped; antivirals - oseltamivir (or zanamivir, baloxavir). Zika: ssRNA (positive-sense), enveloped; no approved antiviral. Ebola: ssRNA (negative-sense), enveloped; antivirals - monoclonal antibody therapies (e.g., ansuvimab, atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab); remdesivir has also been studied.

questions.question: Remdesivir

parts.text: What is its mechanism of action?
What other 2 viruses (other than SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV) has it been shown to have activity in animal studies?

questions.model_answer:
a) Mechanism of action: remdesivir is a prodrug of an adenosine nucleotide analogue; after intracellular metabolism to its active triphosphate form, it is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase into the nascent viral RNA chain, causing delayed chain termination (evading initial proofreading by the viral exonuclease).
b) 2 other viruses shown to have activity in animal studies (other than SARS-CoV/MERS-CoV): Ebola virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (Nipah virus and Marburg virus are also accepted answers).

questions.question: Ebola.

parts.text: 3 places the virus can persist after symptoms resolve

questions.model_answer:
a) Three sites of viral persistence after symptom resolution: (1) testes/semen (can persist many months) (2) eye/aqueous humor (3) central nervous system/CSF (placenta and breast milk are additional accepted sites).
b) Remdesivir mechanism: a nucleotide (adenosine) analog prodrug that is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, causing delayed chain termination and inhibiting viral RNA synthesis.
questions.beyond_mandell: Viral persistence sites and remdesivir mechanism reflect standard virology/pharmacology knowledge beyond this chapter excerpt.
